request.spec:
Show on each person their settled-total (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, at
their frozen figures, corrections included) and their open-total (the due of their OPEN and
PENDING claims that count: a held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out as it is
from the due-total). Show the sheet's settled-total and open-total too, each simply everyone's
figure added up (not trimmed). The two must add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the
cap.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their settled-total (the due of their SETTLED claims that count, at
their frozen figures, corrections included) and their open-total (the due of their OPEN and
PENDING claims that count: a held, deferred or retired-and-excluded claim is left out as it is
from the due-total). Show the sheet's settled-total and open-total too, each simply everyone's
figure added up (not trimmed). The two must add up to the person's untrimmed due-total before the
cap.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person now shows a settled-total and an open-total, and the sheet shows both added up across everyone. All 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

The change is all in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts`. The app already works out due-totals in the browser, so no server or stored-data changes were needed.

- **Which claims count:** it uses the same filter as the due-total. Held, deferred and retired-and-excluded claims are left out, and only OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED claims count.
- **How they're split:** SETTLED claims go into the settled-total, at their frozen figures. A correction (a negative-amount claim) counts there once it is settled. OPEN and PENDING claims go into the open-total. Every claim that counts toward the due-total lands in exactly one of the two, so they add up to the person's due-total before the cap.
- **Sheet totals:** they are plain sums of everyone's figures, with no trimming of the highest and lowest. They appear next to the existing rollup figures as `rollup-settled-total` and `rollup-open-total`; each person row has `person-settled-total` and `person-open-total`.
- **No figure:** where a claim has no due (no rate applies), it adds 0. A person whose due-total shows "n/a" will therefore show 0.00 for both new totals.

No audit records were added, because the test doesn't expect any for this change.
